newsitem.title: UK: Japanese Stocks in London slip but shrug off Deng.
newsitem.headline: Japanese Stocks in London slip but shrug off Deng.

text.p: Japanese stocks in London were generally a touch lower than their Tokyo closing price on Thursday but were largely unaffected by the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, traders said.

The Nikkei 50 index of leading shares traded in London rose some 27.65 points or 1.94 percent from Wednesday's London close to 1,453.77, after the Tokyo Nikkei 225 index ended some 452.59 points or 2.43 percent firmer at 19,051.71.
Automotive and hi-tech stocks saw profit taking, one trader said, but other stocks firmed on the back of a Tokyo rally in property issues.
"People shied from exporters and looked to banks and construction, which gave liquidity to the real estate market," the dealer added.
Banks, which traditionally hold land in their portfolios, were very firm in London, he said, with most trading above their Tokyo close.
Interest was also seen in railway stocks, he added. Like banks, railway companies also traditionally hold land in their portfolios.
Exporter Sharp edged lower after the company announced it would fall two billion yen short of its earning estimates for 1996. It was trading at 1,587.5 yen, down 2.5 yen from its Tokyo close.
